_about: DAY TRACK paper log (docs/day-track-spec.md). One row per trading day the track was evaluated: the trade the run COULD have taken at the quote it actually saw, managed against the bars. Rows share the shape of holdings.json._DAY_TRACK.results plus phase:'paper'. Written by the first run at/after 09:35 ET; exits appended by later runs. Read by day_track.graduate() at the Monday calibration.

opening_range.source: get_equity_historicals(QQQ, interval='minute', bounds='regular') 13:30-13:34Z, all five bars present and settled by 13:35:10Z. ONE-MINUTE bars per spec, never 5-minute buckets.

exit.r_note: RECORDED AT THE STOP PRICE PER SPEC ('later runs ... record exits at the stop / chop / flat prices'), which is -1.00R by construction. THE HONEST FILL IS WORSE AND IS NOT BEING HIDDEN: a resting stop_market on PSQ triggers and then fills AT MARKET, and PSQ's next tick down is 26.16, so the realistic fill is 26.16 -> -$1.96 -> -1.254R. The spec's convention is kept so graduate() reads one consistent statistic across the paper sample and this run does not get to change the track's statistic; the slippage figure is carried here and flagged to the Monday calibration.
exit.day_complete: YES. Spec: 'One day trade per trading day. Stop hit = done for the day.' No re-entry on 2026-09-15 regardless of what QQQ does next.

rows.capital_note: Paper only -- no order placed, none placeable: _DAY_TRACK.status is PAPER and LIVE additionally requires the v11 stamp, while this run was invoked with v10. Sizing used deployable $1,470.86 (unleveraged_buying_power $1,664.60 minus the 5% operational reserve $193.74). rows.bugs_found_and_fixed_by_this_row: Two, both in day_track.plan_entry, both caught only because this was the first SHORT signal the track ever produced. See holdings.json._DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG_INSTRUMENT_2026-09-15.

management.managed_by: scheduled run 13:45Z 2026-09-16 (unattended, prompt v11) -- SECOND post-bell run; the 13:30Z sibling opened this row and left it status 'open', so this run owes it a management pass.

inputs.price_note: The BID, not the 709.835 last. A long position is SOLD INTO THE BID, so the bid is the executable price and the conservative side for any exit-management decision. This follows the sibling's own finding from this same morning, _RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID_ASK_STRADDLES_THE_TRIGGER_PRICE_2026-09-16, applied to the day track rather than to the RSI2 exit. Immaterial here -- last gives 2.465R and bid 2.439R, both clear of the 2.0 trail trigger -- but the habit is the point.
inputs.session_high_source: Max of ONE-MINUTE highs 13:35-13:59Z (the 13:55 bar). Cross-checked against the 5-minute buckets, which agree.

management.feed_integrity_checked_first: ALL THREE 5-minute buckets used here reconcile EXACTLY to their 1-minute sums -- 13:45 bucket 307,199 vs sum 307,199; 13:50 206,329 vs 206,329; 13:55 110,275 vs 110,275. Zero discrepancy, so no feed hole propagates into the stop level. Noted separately: the 13:55 bucket read 104,898 on a 13:59Z fetch and 110,275 on a 14:01Z fetch -- the documented in-progress settling revision, not a hole; both reads agree the bar's HIGH is 710.18, which is the number the trail depends on.
management.both_ratchets_fire_and_the_trail_wins: At 2.44R both thresholds are crossed. Breakeven (r>=1) would move the stop to entry 708.43; the trail (r>=2) gives session_high - 1.5 x ATR5 = 710.18 - 1.23 = 708.95. The stop ratchets UP only and takes the higher: 707.86 -> 708.9500. That locks in +0.52 per share (+0.92R) against the 708.43 entry.
management.PAPER_so_nothing_was_placed: _DAY_TRACK.status is PAPER, so NO stop order was placed or replaced at the broker. In LIVE this pass would be a cancel/replace of the resting stop_market to 708.95 in this same minute. Recorded here so the paper row carries the management history the LIVE phase will have to execute.
management.next_checks: Flat rule at 15:30 ET; chop rule is already moot (|R| >> 0.5). Stop now 708.95. The FOMC decision at 18:00Z falls INSIDE this position's window and the flat rule is 1.5 hours after it -- the sibling flagged this and no gate may be added for it.
management.SUPERSEDED_2026-09-16T14:20Z: This ratchet is VOID as a stop level: the initial stop 707.86 was breached at 13:36Z, 24 minutes before this pass, so there was no live position to ratchet. Kept in full because the pass itself was careful and its ATR5/feed findings stand. See the row's exit.SUPERSEDES_THE_14_00Z_RATCHET_AND_WHY.

stop_history.why: VOID -- reconstructed: stop 707.86 was hit at 13:36Z; the 14:00Z ratchet to 708.95 postdates the exit and never existed.

exit.exited_by: scheduled run 14:00Z 2026-09-16 (unattended, prompt v11), on re-examining the row after a merge conflict with the concurrent 13:45Z run.
exit.evidence: QQQ 1-minute bars (bounds=regular): the 13:36 bar -- the FIRST full minute after the 13:35:30.133Z entry -- printed LOW 707.650 against the initial stop 707.86, a breach of 0.21 points. The 13:39 bar low 707.840 breached again. FETCHED TWICE, ~5 minutes apart (14:02Z and 14:18Z), per the provisional-bar rule: byte-identical both times (o 708.200 / h 708.215 / l 707.650 / c 708.072, vol 102,727), so the bar is settled and not a revision artifact. Feed integrity: the 13:35Z five-minute bucket volume 455,774 equals its 1-minute sum 83,954+102,727+95,313+81,243+92,537 exactly, and the bucket low equals the 1-minute minimum. SPY pulled in the same call as a cross-symbol control printed normally across the identical timestamps.
exit.r_note: RECORDED AT THE STOP PRICE (-1.00R = -$0.57) per spec, the same convention paper day 1 used, so graduate() reads one consistent statistic. The honest fill is worse and is not hidden: a resting stop_market at 707.86 triggers and fills at market, and the breaching minute traded to 707.650, so a realistic fill is 707.65-707.86 -> -1.00R to -1.37R. day_track.manage() fed the actual bar low returns r=-1.368.
exit.day_complete: YES -- one day trade per trading day, stop hit. No re-entry on 2026-09-16 whatever QQQ does next.
exit.SUPERSEDES_THE_14_00Z_RATCHET_AND_WHY: The concurrent 13:45Z run's management pass (preserved in full in this row's 'management' array, and NOT deleted) ratcheted the stop 707.86 -> 708.95 at +2.44R and left status 'open'. That pass was correct in every step it took and is wrong in its conclusion, because the position it managed had already stopped 24 minutes earlier. A stop cannot ratchet after it has been hit, so the 708.95 level never existed and the row's outcome is -1.00R, not an open winner. The 2.44R figure, the ATR5 measurement and the finding it produced (_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_MOSTLY_YESTERDAY_2026-09-16) are all independently valid and are kept. Root cause, and it is the durable lesson: _DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_THE_ADVERSE_EXTREME_SINCE_THE_LAST_PASS_NOT_THE_CURRENT_PRICE_2026-09-16.
exit.counterfactual_not_a_result: QQQ traded 710.01 at 14:01:05Z. Had the stop not been taken the position would be ~+2.8R. THIS IS A LIVE MARK, NOT A RESULT. It is recorded only because it is the second consecutive paper day on which the DIRECTION was right and the stop was removed by sub-2-minute noise -- see _DAY_TRACK_BOTH_PAPER_SIGNALS_WERE_DIRECTIONALLY_RIGHT_AND_BOTH_STOPPED_INSIDE_TWO_MINUTES_2026-09-16.
